sources.snippet: + 5.4 Steamworks on PlayStation 3. + 6.1 Users and revenue. + 6.2 Sales and distribution. | The Steam storefront as of November 2025 |. **Steam** is a digital distribution platform for PC games by the American video game studio Valve. It was launched as a software client in September 2003 to provide video game updates automatically for Valve's games and expanded to distributing third-party titles in late 2005. Initially developed for Windows, Steam was ported to macOS and Linux in 2010 and 2013 respectively, while a mobile version of Steam for interacting with the service's online features was released on iOS and Android "Android (operating system)") in 2012. Steam's success has led to the development of the Steam Machine "Steam Machine (computer)") gaming PCs in 2015, including the SteamOS Linux distribution and Steam Controller "Steam Controller (2015)"); Steam Link devices for local game streaming; and in 2022, the handheld Steam Deck tailored for running Steam games.

sources.snippet: Go to Windows platform Display platforms icon. ## The quintessential PC video game platform. **Steam** is the official client for Valve's digital distribution service. This platform, whose first official version was released in 2003, features a colossal catalog of video games, including a great number of completely free titles that you can download and play with ease. To give you some idea of just how big Steam is, more than 19,000 games were published in 2025 alone, the vast majority of them paid. In order to purchase and download games on Steam, you need to register. Best of all, although the bulk of all releases are paid titles, you can also download a great number of video games for free. The platform not only offers a way to stay in constant contact with friends and acquaintances where you can chat or leave comments, it also has online leaderboards, achievements, collectible cards, prizes, and much more.
